public_rationale: GitHub's implementation establishes one transition, while Anthropic's reported pause shows that an announced change need not take effect. Neither establishes the share of the overall market. No qualifying majority census or other conclusive event was found. The forecast remains open because it has no deadline.
limitations: The result could depend on whether offerings, plans, providers, or subscribers are counted.
Examples from prominent providers are not a market-wide measurement.
The Anthropic pause is documented here through a news report.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The majority of AI subscriptions will inevitably move to token-based billing.

statement.excerpt: I think it’s inevitable that the majority of AI subscriptions move to token-based billing, especially as both Anthropic and OpenAI have now done so with their enterprise customers.
statement.document_title: AI's Economics Don't Make Sense [Ad Free]

our_interpretation: The primary reading counts distinct paid LLM subscription offerings, rather than revenue or subscriber seats. The wording does not specify the denominator.
A transition counts when token consumption determines the paid allowance or additional charges. A message cap alone does not count.
A subscription fee bundled with token credits can count as token-based billing; retaining a monthly fee does not automatically exclude it.
The statement supplies no deadline. Its reference to enterprise changes is supporting context, not a condition.
criteria.support_condition: A documented market-wide census shows that more than half of in-scope paid subscription offerings have transitioned from non-token billing to token-based billing.
criteria.contradiction_condition: With no deadline, persistence of flat subscriptions at a finite date cannot contradict inevitability. Contradiction would require a decisive event making the predicted majority transition impossible.
